
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Unisci tutti e quattro i dataset in un unico dataframe master
combined_gather_data <- bind_rows(
  RCC_1808J_gather,
  RCC154B_gather,
  RCC1477_gather,
  RCC_162_gather,
  RCC1466_gather
)

# 2. Esegui la pipeline sui dati combinati e crea il grafico
my_plot <- combined_gather_data %>%
  # Pulisci la colonna 'name' per estrarre solo Genere e Specie
  mutate(species_name = word(name, 2, 3)) %>%
  
  # Raggruppa per 'query_name' (che separa i 4 campioni) e specie
  group_by(query_name, species_name) %>%
  
  # Collassa i ceppi prendendo il MASSIMO della 'median_abund'
  summarise(true_abundance = max(median_abund), .groups = "drop") %>%
  
  # Filtra il rumore di fondo assoluto

  # 3. Costruisci il grafico
  # reorder_within ordina le barre correttamente all'interno di ogni pannello
  ggplot(aes(x = tidytext::reorder_within(species_name, true_abundance, query_name), y = true_abundance)) +
  
  # Usa le colonne per rappresentare l'abbondanza
  geom_col(alpha = 0.8, fill = "steelblue") +
  
  # Aggiungi la linea rossa tratteggiata per la soglia di contaminazione
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  
  # Ruota le coordinate per leggere i nomi delle specie
  coord_flip() +
  
  # Rimuove i nomi dei campioni aggiunti da reorder_within dalle etichette degli assi
  tidytext::scale_x_reordered() +
  
  # Scala logaritmica per l'asse Y (che visivamente diventa l'asse orizzontale)
  ylim(0, 4000) + 
  
  # DIVIDI PER CAMPIONE E IMPILA VERTICALMENTE (ncol = 1 invece di nrow = 1)
  facet_wrap(~ query_name, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  
  # Pulisci le etichette e il tema
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Profili di Abbondanza delle Specie (Isolati vs Contaminati)",
    x = "Specie",
    y = "Profondità di Sequenziamento (Max median_abund)"
  )

# Mostra il grafico su schermo
print(my_plot)

# SUGGERIMENTO: Poiché ci sono 4 grafici impilati, potrebbero sembrare schiacciati
# nel viewer di RStudio. Usa questo comando per salvare un'immagine ad alta risoluzione 
# dando abbastanza "altezza" (height) al file:
# ggsave("profili_abbondanza.png", plot = my_plot, width = 10, height = 12, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidytext) 

# 1. LOAD YOUR DATA
df <- bind_rows(RCC1477_species_summary, RCC1808J_csv_summarized , species_summary_csv_summarized,RCC1466_csv_summarized,RCC162_csv_summarized, RCC312_csv_summarized , RCC1714_csv_summarized)
plot_data <- df %>%
  filter(rank == "species") %>%
  mutate(
    clean_species = case_when(
      lineage == "unclassified" ~ "Unclassified",
      TRUE ~ str_replace(str_extract(lineage, "s__.*$"), "s__", "")
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    clean_species = if_else(f_weighted_at_rank < 0.01, "Other (< 1%)", clean_species)
  ) %>%
  group_by(query_name, clean_species) %>%
  summarize(f_weighted_at_rank = sum(f_weighted_at_rank), .groups = "drop") %>%
  
  filter(clean_species != "Unclassified")

ggplot(plot_data, aes(
    x = f_weighted_at_rank, 
    y = reorder_within(clean_species, f_weighted_at_rank, query_name), 
    fill = clean_species
  )) +
  
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.05, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 0.8) +
  
  geom_col(color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) + 
  facet_wrap(~ query_name, scales = "free", ncol = 1) + 
  
  # Lock the X-axis from 0 to 1 (100%) so the 95% line is always in the same place
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_y_reordered() + 
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"), 
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    legend.position = "none", 
    panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines"), 
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12) 
  )
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
# install.packages("ggrepel") if not already installed
library(ggrepel)
quast <- read_tsv("assembly_benchmark.tsv")

quast_long <- quast %>%
  pivot_longer(-Assembly, names_to = "sample", values_to = "value") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Assembly, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(across(-sample, ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.))))

quast_long <- quast_long %>%
  mutate(method = case_when(
    str_detect(sample, "shovill") ~ "shovill",
    str_detect(sample, "seqkit")  ~ "seqkit",
    str_detect(sample, "bbnorm")  ~ "bbnorm",
    sample == "megahit"           ~ "megahit",
    TRUE ~ "other"
  ))

key_metrics <- c("# contigs", "Genome fraction (%)", "NGA50",
                  "# misassemblies", "# mismatches per 100 kbp",
                  "Duplication ratio")

plot_df <- quast_long %>%
  select(sample, method, all_of(key_metrics)) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(key_metrics), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value")

p1 <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = reorder(sample, value), y = value, fill = method)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "QUAST comparison — key metrics") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
p1

##ggsave("quast_key_metrics.png", p1, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)

# --- Plot 2: contiguity vs. accuracy trade-off ---------------------------
# This is usually the more decisive view: assemblies in the top-left
# (high NGA50, low misassemblies) are the strongest candidates.
p2 <- ggplot(quast_long,
              aes(x = NGA50, y = `# misassemblies`,
                  color = method, size = `Genome fraction (%)`)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = sample), size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "NGA50 (bp) — higher = more contiguous",
       y = "# misassemblies — lower = more accurate",
       size = "Genome fraction (%)",
       title = "Contiguity vs. accuracy trade-off") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
p2
#ggsave("quast_tradeoff.png", p2, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

quast <- read_tsv("assembly_benchmark.tsv")

quast_long <- quast %>%
  pivot_longer(-Assembly, names_to = "sample", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(
    method = case_when(
      str_detect(sample, "shovill") ~ "shovill",
      str_detect(sample, "seqkit")  ~ "seqkit",
      str_detect(sample, "bbnorm")  ~ "bbnorm",
      sample == "megahit"           ~ "megahit",
      TRUE ~ "other"
    ),
    # pulls the leading number out of each cell -> handles "-" (NA50/NGA90 etc,
    # becomes NA) and composite values like "8 + 23 part" (becomes 8) in one go
    value = as.numeric(str_extract(value, "^-?[0-9.]+"))
  ) %>%
  drop_na(value)

ggplot(quast_long, aes(x = sample, y = value, color = method)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ Assembly, scales = "free_y", ncol = 6) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 6.5, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = unit(0.6, "lines"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

quast <- read_tsv("assembly_benchmark.tsv")

quast_long <- quast %>%
  pivot_longer(-Assembly, names_to = "sample", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(
    method = case_when(
      str_detect(sample, "shovill") ~ "shovill",
      str_detect(sample, "seqkit")  ~ "seqkit",
      str_detect(sample, "bbnorm")  ~ "bbnorm",
      sample == "megahit"           ~ "megahit",
      TRUE ~ "other"
    ),
    # pulls the leading number out of each cell -> handles "-" (NA50/NGA90 etc,
    # becomes NA) and composite values like "8 + 23 part" (becomes 8) in one go
    value = as.numeric(str_extract(value, "^-?[0-9.]+"))
  ) %>%
  drop_na(value)

# Reference length and Reference GC (%) are excluded below: they're constant
# across every assembly (same reference used for all), so they carry no
# comparative signal.

contiguity_metrics <- c(
  "# contigs (>= 0 bp)", "# contigs (>= 1000 bp)", "# contigs (>= 5000 bp)",
  "# contigs (>= 10000 bp)", "# contigs (>= 25000 bp)", "# contigs (>= 50000 bp)",
  "# contigs", "Largest contig",
  "Total length (>= 0 bp)", "Total length (>= 1000 bp)", "Total length (>= 5000 bp)",
  "Total length (>= 10000 bp)", "Total length (>= 25000 bp)", "Total length (>= 50000 bp)",
  "Total length",
  "N50", "NG50", "N90", "NG90", "auN", "auNG", "L50", "LG50", "L90", "LG90"
)

accuracy_metrics <- c(
  "# misassemblies", "# misassembled contigs", "Misassembled contigs length",
  "# local misassemblies", "# scaffold gap ext. mis.", "# scaffold gap loc. mis.",
  "# unaligned mis. contigs", "# mismatches per 100 kbp", "# indels per 100 kbp",
  "# N's per 100 kbp", "GC (%)"
)

alignment_metrics <- c(
  "Genome fraction (%)", "Duplication ratio", "# unaligned contigs", "Unaligned length",
  "Largest alignment", "Total aligned length",
  "NA50", "NGA50", "NA90", "NGA90", "auNA", "auNGA", "LA50", "LGA50", "LA90", "LGA90"
)

plot_metric_group <- function(df, metrics, ncol = 4) {
  ggplot(filter(df, Assembly %in% metrics), aes(x = sample, y = value, color = method)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.8) +
    facet_wrap(~ Assembly, scales = "free_y", ncol = ncol) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, color = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 7.5, face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing = unit(0.6, "lines"),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )
}

plot_metric_group(quast_long, contiguity_metrics, ncol = 5)

plot_metric_group(quast_long, accuracy_metrics, ncol = 4)

plot_metric_group(quast_long, alignment_metrics, ncol = 4)

```
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# ---- 1. Read all three TSVs and tag each with its genome sample name -----
# NOTE: adjust the filename/label for Sample 3 to match your actual file.

quast_1 <- read_tsv("assembly_benchmark.tsv") %>%
  mutate(genome_sample = "Sample 1")

quast_2 <- read_tsv("assembly_benchmarkRCC162.tsv") %>%
  mutate(genome_sample = "Sample 2")

quast_3 <- read_tsv("assembly_benchmarkRCC312.tsv") %>%
  mutate(genome_sample = "Sample 3")

quast <- bind_rows(quast_1, quast_2, quast_3)

# ---- 2. Reshape to long format --------------------------------------------
# Note: `sample` here is your assembler/depth column (e.g. "seqkit_100x"),
# NOT the genome sample. Keep that naming as-is so the rest of your pipeline
# still works; `genome_sample` is the new axis we're adding.

quast_long <- quast %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(Assembly, genome_sample), names_to = "sample", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(
    method = case_when(
      str_detect(sample, "shovill") ~ sample,
      str_detect(sample, "seqkit")  ~ sample,
      str_detect(sample, "bbnorm")  ~ sample,
      sample == "megahit"           ~ "megahit",
      TRUE ~ "other"
    ),
    value = as.numeric(str_extract(value, "^-?[0-9.]+"))
  ) %>%
  drop_na(value)

# ---- 3. Metric groupings (unchanged from your original script) -----------

contiguity_metrics <- c(
  "# contigs (>= 0 bp)", "# contigs (>= 1000 bp)", "# contigs (>= 5000 bp)",
  "# contigs (>= 10000 bp)", "# contigs (>= 25000 bp)", "# contigs (>= 50000 bp)",
  "# contigs", "Largest contig",
  "Total length (>= 0 bp)", "Total length (>= 1000 bp)", "Total length (>= 5000 bp)",
  "Total length (>= 10000 bp)", "Total length (>= 25000 bp)", "Total length (>= 50000 bp)",
  "Total length",
  "N50", "NG50", "N90", "NG90", "auN", "auNG", "L50", "LG50", "L90", "LG90"
)

accuracy_metrics <- c(
  "# misassemblies", "# misassembled contigs", "Misassembled contigs length",
  "# local misassemblies", "# scaffold gap ext. mis.", "# scaffold gap loc. mis.",
  "# unaligned mis. contigs", "# mismatches per 100 kbp", "# indels per 100 kbp",
  "# N's per 100 kbp", "GC (%)"
)

alignment_metrics <- c(
  "Genome fraction (%)", "Duplication ratio", "# unaligned contigs", "Unaligned length",
  "Largest alignment", "Total aligned length",
  "NA50", "NGA50", "NA90", "NGA90", "auNA", "auNGA", "LA50", "LGA50", "LA90", "LGA90"
)

ref_df <- quast_all %>%
  distinct(genome_sample, `Reference length`, `Reference GC (%)`) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(`Reference length`, `Reference GC (%)`),
    names_to = "Assembly", values_to = "ref_value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Assembly = recode(Assembly,
                            "Reference length"   = "Total length",
                            "Reference GC (%)"   = "GC (%)"),
         Assembly = factor(Assembly, levels = core_metrics))

# ---- 4. Plotting function: facet_grid(Assembly ~ genome_sample) ----------
# Rows = metric, Columns = genome sample. With a third sample this now
# produces three columns per metric row, so you can compare all three
# samples at a glance for every metric while still seeing per-assembler
# spread within each sample.

plot_metric_group <- function(df, metrics, ncol_metrics = 4) {
  ggplot(filter(df, Assembly %in% metrics),
         aes(x = method, y = value, color = method)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.8) +
    facet_grid(Assembly ~ genome_sample, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, color = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      strip.text.y = element_text(size = 7, face = "bold", angle = 0),
      strip.text.x = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing = unit(0.5, "lines"),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )
}

plot_metric_group_overlay <- function(df, metrics, ncol = 4) {
  ggplot(filter(df, Assembly %in% metrics),
         aes(x = sample, y = value, color = method, shape = genome_sample)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.8) +
    facet_wrap(~ Assembly, scales = "free_y", ncol = ncol) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, color = NULL, shape = "Genome sample") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 7.5, face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing = unit(0.6, "lines"),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )
}

plot_metric_group_overlay(quast_long, contiguity_metrics, ncol = 5)
ggsave("quast_contiguity_overlay.png", p_contiguity_overlay, width = 16, height = 10, dpi = 300)

plot_metric_group_overlay(quast_long, accuracy_metrics, ncol = 4)
ggsave("quast_accuracy_overlay.png", p_accuracy_overlay, width = 13, height = 8, dpi = 300)

plot_metric_group_overlay(quast_long, alignment_metrics, ncol = 4)
ggsave("quast_alignment_overlay.png", p_alignment_overlay, width = 13, height = 10, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# ---- 1. Read all three TSVs, tag with genome sample, compute derived metrics ----

read_and_derive <- function(path, sample_label) {
  read_tsv(path) %>%
    pivot_longer(-Assembly, names_to = "sample", values_to = "value") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Assembly, values_from = value) %>%
    mutate(across(-sample, ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.)))) %>%
    mutate(
      method = case_when(
        str_detect(sample, "shovill") ~ sample,
        str_detect(sample, "seqkit")  ~ sample,
        str_detect(sample, "bbnorm")  ~ sample,
        sample == "megahit"           ~ "megahit",
        TRUE ~ "other"
      ),
      `Aligned fraction (%)`           = 100 * `Total aligned length` / `Total length`,
      `Misassemblies / 100 Mb aligned` = `# misassemblies` * 100 / (`Total aligned length` / 1e6),
      genome_sample = sample_label
    )
}

quast_1 <- read_and_derive("assembly_benchmark.tsv", "Sample 1")
quast_2 <- read_and_derive("assembly_benchmarkRCC162.tsv", "Sample 2")
quast_3 <- read_and_derive("assembly_benchmarkRCC312.tsv", "Sample 3")

quast_all <- bind_rows(quast_1, quast_2, quast_3)

core_metrics <- c(
  "NGA50",
  "Genome fraction (%)",
  "Aligned fraction (%)",
  "Misassemblies / 100 Mb aligned",
  "# mismatches per 100 kbp",
  "# indels per 100 kbp",
  "Duplication ratio",
  "Total length",
  "GC (%)"
)

quast_long <- quast_all %>%
  select(sample, method, genome_sample, all_of(core_metrics)) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(core_metrics), names_to = "Assembly", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(Assembly = factor(Assembly, levels = core_metrics))

# ---- 3. Reference values (one per genome sample), reshaped to match the
#          "Total length" / "GC (%)" facets so geom_hline lands on the right panel ----
ref_df <- quast_all %>%
  distinct(genome_sample, `Reference length`, `Reference GC (%)`) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(`Reference length`, `Reference GC (%)`),
    names_to = "Assembly", values_to = "ref_value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Assembly = recode(Assembly,
                            "Reference length"   = "Total length",
                            "Reference GC (%)"   = "GC (%)"),
         Assembly = factor(Assembly, levels = core_metrics))

# ---- 4. Overlay plot ----
p_core_overlay <- ggplot(quast_long,
       aes(x = sample, y = value, color = method, shape = genome_sample)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_hline(
    data = ref_df,
    aes(yintercept = ref_value, linetype = genome_sample),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ Assembly, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, color = NULL,
       shape = "Genome sample", linetype = "Genome sample",
       title = "Core reference-based assembly benchmarking metrics — overlay across samples") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = unit(0.6, "lines"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

p_core_overlay

# ggsave("quast_core_overlay.png", p_core_overlay, width = 12, height = 10, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
quast_1 <- read_tsv("report.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(genome_sample = "Sample 1")

quast_2 <- read_tsv("assembly_benchmarkRCC162.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(genome_sample = "Sample 2")

quast_3 <- read_tsv("assembly_benchmarkRCC312.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(genome_sample = "Sample 3")

quast <- bind_rows(quast_1, quast_2, quast_3)

# ---- 2. Reshape to long format --------------------------------------------
quast_long <- quast %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(Assembly, genome_sample), names_to = "sample", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(
    method = case_when(
      str_detect(sample, "shovill") ~ sample,
      str_detect(sample, "seqkit")  ~ sample,
      str_detect(sample, "bbnorm")  ~ sample,
      sample == "megahit"           ~ "megahit",
      TRUE ~ "other"
    ),
    value = as.numeric(str_extract(value, "^-?[0-9.]+"))
  ) %>%
  drop_na(value)

# ---- 3. Metric groupings --------------------------------------------------
contiguity_metrics <- c(
  "# contigs", "Largest contig",
  "Total length")

accuracy_metrics <- c(
  "# misassemblies", "# misassembled contigs", "Misassembled contigs length",
  "# local misassemblies", "# scaffold gap ext. mis.", "# scaffold gap loc. mis.",
  "# unaligned mis. contigs", "# mismatches per 100 kbp", "# indels per 100 kbp",
  "# N's per 100 kbp", "GC (%)"
)

alignment_metrics <- c(
  "Genome fraction (%)", "Duplication ratio", "# unaligned contigs", "Unaligned length",
  "Largest alignment", "Total aligned length",
  "NA50", "NGA50", "NA90", "NGA90", "auNA", "auNGA", "LA50", "LGA50", "LA90", "LGA90"
)


ref_df <- quast_long %>%
  filter(Assembly %in% c("Reference length", "Reference GC (%)")) %>%
  distinct(genome_sample, Assembly, value) %>%
  select(genome_sample, Assembly, ref_value = value) %>%
  mutate(Assembly = recode(Assembly,
                           "Reference length"   = "Total length",
                           "Reference GC (%)"   = "GC (%)")) %>%
  drop_na(ref_value)

plot_metric_group_overlay <- function(df, metrics, ref_data, ncol = 4) {
  
  plot_data <- filter(df, Assembly %in% metrics)
  current_refs <- filter(ref_data, Assembly %in% metrics)
  
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = sample, y = value, color = method, shape = genome_sample)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.8, alpha = 0.8) +
    facet_wrap(~ Assembly, scales = "free_y", ncol = ncol) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, color = NULL, shape = "Genome sample", linetype = "Genome sample") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 7.5, face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing = unit(0.6, "lines"),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )
  
  if (nrow(current_refs) > 0) {
    p <- p + geom_hline(
      data = current_refs,
      aes(yintercept = ref_value, linetype = genome_sample),
      color = "red", linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.6
    )
  }
  
  return(p)
}


# 1. Contiguity 
p_contiguity_overlay <- plot_metric_group_overlay(quast_long, contiguity_metrics, ref_df, ncol = 5)
print(p_contiguity_overlay)
ggsave("quast_contiguity_overlay.png", p_contiguity_overlay, width = 16, height = 10, dpi = 300)

# 2. Accuracy 
p_accuracy_overlay <- plot_metric_group_overlay(quast_long, accuracy_metrics, ref_df, ncol = 4)
print(p_accuracy_overlay)
ggsave("quast_accuracy_overlay.png", p_accuracy_overlay, width = 13, height = 8, dpi = 300)

# 3. Alignment 
p_alignment_overlay <- plot_metric_group_overlay(quast_long, alignment_metrics, ref_df, ncol = 4)
print(p_alignment_overlay)
ggsave("quast_alignment_overlay.png", p_alignment_overlay, width = 13, height = 10, dpi = 300)
```
```{r}
#   NGA50 (falls back to NA50 if missing)              -> higher is better
#   Genome fraction (%)                                 -> higher is better
#   Aligned assembly fraction (Total aligned length
#       / Total length)                                 -> higher is better
#   Misassemblies per 100 Mb                             -> lower is better
#   Mismatches + indels per 100 kbp                       -> lower is better
#   Duplication ratio (deviation from 1)                   -> lower is better
#   Total length vs Reference length (deviation from 1)      -> lower is better
#
# SCORING
#   For each of the 7 metrics above, whichever assembler has the best value
#   (accounting for direction) wins 1 point for that category (ties all
#   get a point). Points are summed across all 7 categories, and the
#   assembler with the most points overall is reported as the winner.
#
```


```{r}
input_file <- "assembly_benchmarkRCC762.tsv"   # <-- change this to your file's path
metric_col <- "Assembly"              # column holding QUAST metric names


sep <- if (grepl("\\.tsv$", input_file, ignore.case = TRUE)) "\t" else ","
df <- read.delim(input_file, sep = sep, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                  check.names = FALSE)

if (!(metric_col %in% names(df))) {
  stop("Couldn't find a '", metric_col, "' column. Found: ",
       paste(names(df), collapse = ", "))
}

asm_cols <- setdiff(names(df), metric_col)

row_nga50 <- df[df[[metric_col]] == "NGA50", asm_cols]
nga50 <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("\\s*\\+.*$", "", trimws(as.character(row_nga50[1, ])))))
names(nga50) <- asm_cols

row_na50 <- df[df[[metric_col]] == "NA50", asm_cols]
na50 <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("\\s*\\+.*$", "", trimws(as.character(row_na50[1, ])))))
names(na50) <- asm_cols
nga50[is.na(nga50)] <- na50[is.na(nga50)]   

row_gf <- df[df[[metric_col]] == "Genome fraction (%)", asm_cols]
genome_fraction <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(trimws(as.character(row_gf[1, ]))))
names(genome_fraction) <- asm_cols

row_tl <- df[df[[metric_col]] == "Total length", asm_cols]
total_length <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(trimws(as.character(row_tl[1, ]))))
names(total_length) <- asm_cols

row_rl <- df[df[[metric_col]] == "Reference length", asm_cols]
reference_length <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(trimws(as.character(row_rl[1, ]))))
names(reference_length) <- asm_cols

row_tal <- df[df[[metric_col]] == "Total aligned length", asm_cols]
total_aligned_length <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(trimws(as.character(row_tal[1, ]))))
names(total_aligned_length) <- asm_cols

row_mis <- df[df[[metric_col]] == "# misassemblies", asm_cols]
n_misassemblies <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(trimws(as.character(row_mis[1, ]))))
names(n_misassemblies) <- asm_cols

row_mm <- df[df[[metric_col]] == "# mismatches per 100 kbp", asm_cols]
mismatches_100kbp <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(trimws(as.character(row_mm[1, ]))))
names(mismatches_100kbp) <- asm_cols

row_indel <- df[df[[metric_col]] == "# indels per 100 kbp", asm_cols]
indels_100kbp <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(trimws(as.character(row_indel[1, ]))))
names(indels_100kbp) <- asm_cols

row_dup <- df[df[[metric_col]] == "Duplication ratio", asm_cols]
duplication_ratio <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(trimws(as.character(row_dup[1, ]))))
names(duplication_ratio) <- asm_cols

aligned_fraction        <- total_aligned_length / total_length
misassemblies_per_100Mb <- n_misassemblies / (total_length / 1e8)
base_error_per_100kbp    <- mismatches_100kbp + indels_100kbp
duplication_ratio_dev     <- abs(duplication_ratio - 1)
length_vs_reference_dev      <- abs(total_length / reference_length - 1)

points <- rep(0, length(asm_cols))
names(points) <- asm_cols

best_val <- suppressWarnings(max(nga50, na.rm = TRUE))
winners <- names(nga50)[!is.na(nga50) & nga50 == best_val]
points[winners] <- points[winners] + 1

best_val <- suppressWarnings(max(genome_fraction, na.rm = TRUE))
winners <- names(genome_fraction)[!is.na(genome_fraction) & genome_fraction == best_val]
points[winners] <- points[winners] + 1

best_val <- suppressWarnings(max(aligned_fraction, na.rm = TRUE))
winners <- names(aligned_fraction)[!is.na(aligned_fraction) & aligned_fraction == best_val]
points[winners] <- points[winners] + 1


best_val <- suppressWarnings(min(misassemblies_per_100Mb, na.rm = TRUE))
winners <- names(misassemblies_per_100Mb)[!is.na(misassemblies_per_100Mb) & misassemblies_per_100Mb == best_val]
points[winners] <- points[winners] + 1

best_val <- suppressWarnings(min(base_error_per_100kbp, na.rm = TRUE))
winners <- names(base_error_per_100kbp)[!is.na(base_error_per_100kbp) & base_error_per_100kbp == best_val]
points[winners] <- points[winners] + 1


best_val <- suppressWarnings(min(duplication_ratio_dev, na.rm = TRUE))
winners <- names(duplication_ratio_dev)[!is.na(duplication_ratio_dev) & duplication_ratio_dev == best_val]
points[winners] <- points[winners] + 1

best_val <- suppressWarnings(min(length_vs_reference_dev, na.rm = TRUE))
winners <- names(length_vs_reference_dev)[!is.na(length_vs_reference_dev) & length_vs_reference_dev == best_val]
points[winners] <- points[winners] + 1


res <- data.frame(
  Assembler                = asm_cols,
  NGA50                    = nga50,
  genome_fraction           = genome_fraction,
  aligned_fraction           = round(aligned_fraction, 4),
  misassemblies_per_100Mb     = round(misassemblies_per_100Mb, 1),
  base_error_per_100kbp         = round(base_error_per_100kbp, 2),
  duplication_ratio_dev           = round(duplication_ratio_dev, 4),
  length_vs_reference_dev            = round(length_vs_reference_dev, 5),
  Points                                = points,
  row.names = NULL
)
res <- res[order(-res$Points), ]
print(res, row.names = FALSE)

best <- res[which.max(res$Points), ]
cat(sprintf("\n>>> Best assembler: %s (%d / 7 categories won)\n",
            best$Assembler, best$Points))

out_file <- paste0(tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(input_file)), "_scores.csv")
write.csv(res, out_file, row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nWrote:", out_file, "\n")
```
```{r}


scores_dir   <- "."                    # folder containing the *_scores.csv files
file_pattern <- "_scores\\.csv$"       # regex matching the per-sample score files


score_files <- list.files(scores_dir, pattern = file_pattern, full.names = TRUE)


all_points <- data.frame(Assembler = character(0), Sample = character(0),
                          Points = numeric(0))

for (f in score_files) {
  df <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)

  if (!("Assembler" %in% names(df)) || !("Points" %in% names(df))) {
    warning("Skipping '", basename(f), "': missing 'Assembler' or 'Points' column")
    next
  }

  sample_name <- sub(file_pattern, "", basename(f))

  all_points <- rbind(all_points, data.frame(
    Assembler = df$Assembler,
    Sample    = sample_name,
    Points    = df$Points
  ))
}

wide <- reshape(all_points, idvar = "Assembler", timevar = "Sample",
                 direction = "wide")
names(wide) <- sub("^Points\\.", "", names(wide))

sample_cols <- setdiff(names(wide), "Assembler")
wide$TotalPoints <- rowSums(wide[, sample_cols, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)

wide <- wide[order(-wide$TotalPoints), ]

print(wide, row.names = FALSE)

best <- wide[which.max(wide$TotalPoints), ]
cat(sprintf("\n>>> Overall best assembler: %s (%d total points across %d sample file(s))\n",
            best$Assembler, best$TotalPoints, length(sample_cols)))
```
